title: Locality-aware prefetch topology (personal draft)
content:
Personal scratchpad: locality-aware prefetch topology

Context and motivation
- I'm sketching a lightweight approach to prefetching session/context for multi-tenant inference where locality (region, GPU pool, tenant affinity) matters for both cost and tail latency.
- Goal: reduce cold-token latency and KV cache misses for interactive sessions while limiting wasted tokens on prefetches. Needs to play nicely with dedicated pools (tenant pinned) and shared pools (region/availability-zone aware).
- This is informal — experiments first, spec later. Use as a reference when prototyping an ingress-side prefetcher and small runtime hints.

High-level idea
- Maintain a small per-tenant+route 'hotspot index' (approx sketch) that estimates recent token-prefixes or prompt families that are likely to be reused in the next N seconds.
- Use a topology-aware scheduler to decide where to hydrate prefetched KV caches (same machine, same rack, remote warm pool).
- Choices: inline prefetch (ingress proxies request short prefetch before user requests) vs background prefetch daemon that watches session activity stream.

Design constraints
- Cost-sensitive: limit average prefetch tokens per active session below a configurable budget (default 40 tokens/session/minute).
- Privacy: prefetch must not leak content across tenants; operate on hashed/salting of prompt fingerprint.
- Consistency: if a model variant upgrades, prefetched KV must be invalidated.
- Backpressure: prefetcher should clamp under high CPU/GPU contention.

Topology sketches (ascii)
- Simple rack-local preference:

  ingress -> local-proxy (prefetcher) -> GPU-node-A (same rack)
                       |
                       -> warm-pool (other rack)

- Multi-tier warm pools (fast warm, slow warm). policy decides depth.

Prefetch hint API (proto-ish shape)
- Client-facing (from ingress to runtime):
  {
    "prefetch_hint_id": "string",             // opaque id for tracking
    "tenant_id": "string",                   // tenant / customer id
    "route": "string",                       // Redwood API route or model route
    "fingerprint": "hex64",                 // prompt fingerprint (salted)
    "max_tokens": "int",                    // tokens to prefetch (budgeted)
    "priority": "hot|warm|background",       // scheduling hint
    "affinity": "prefer-local|rack-local|none",
    "ttl_seconds": "int"                    // how long the warmed state is valid
  }

- Notes: keep the schema tiny. Runtime then maps hints to specific hydration steps. Fingerprint must be non-reversible (HMAC).

Prefetcher scheduling heuristics
- Thermostat-inspired priority: maintain a sliding-window of request arrivals per fingerprint. If arrivals exceed threshold T within window W, mark as "hot".
- Decay score with exponential backoff.
- Budgeted eviction: lowest score warm entries are evicted first when capacity hit. Prefer removing warm (rack remote) entries before local ones.
- Admission control: only admit if (expected hit_rate * expected_saved_latency_cost) > cost_of_prefetch. Estimators seeded with offline sims.

Telemetry signals to collect (minimal first pass)
- prefetch_attempts_total, prefetch_success_total, prefetch_waste_tokens_total
- hit_latency_reduction_ms (histogram)
- per-fingerprint arrival_rate, score, warm_pool_size_by_tier
- prefetch_admit_reject_reason (enum: budget, contention, privacy, model_mismatch)

Config example (YAML sketch)
- prefetch:
    enabled: true
    global_token_budget_per_min_per_tenant: 40
    tiers:
      - name: local_fast
        capacity: 1000
        cost_multiplier: 1.0
      - name: rack_warm
        capacity: 5000
        cost_multiplier: 0.25
      - name: remote_cold
        capacity: 20000
        cost_multiplier: 0.05
    admission_threshold: 0.15  # expected saved latency / token cost

Rollout plan (experiment-first)
- Phase 0: offline replay against recent traffic to get baseline hit rates and token waste. Link dataset: JIRA-INF-7213
- Phase 1: shadow prefetcher (no actual prefetch), produce signals and simulate savings.
- Phase 2: limited rollouts to dev tenants with explicit opt-in and budget cap.
- Phase 3: escalate to more tenants, tune heuristics, add rack-aware decisions.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to represent prompt families? LSH-style nearest neighbor vs simple ngram fingerprinting. Tradeoffs: complexity vs privacy.
- Should prefetch hints be signed by control plane to avoid client spoofing? Likely yes for dedicated pools.
- How to integrate with existing KV cache eviction (runtime currently exposes eviction hooks) — need a small API on runtime to accept prefetch token streams vs direct KV blobs.
- Can we piggyback on existing telemetry collection (prom + custom traces) or add a separate lightweight counter stream?

Small experiment ideas
- Replay: pick 72h of chat sessions, simulate a prefetch budget of 30 tokens/min, compute hit-rate and median tail reduction for top 10% sessions.
- Micro benchmark: measure time to hydrate KV for 1k token-prefix on local node vs remote warm pool.
- A/B test UI: opt-in tenants see latency and cost dashboard.

Quick notes to self
- Keep the API tiny. Hints are advisory. Runtime mapping must be policy-driven and reversible (so we can rollback without schema changes).
- Focus on telemetry that proves value: saved-ms-per-prefetch-token. If this metric is weak, kill the feature.
- For privacy: always hash fingerprints with tenant-specific salt and throw away raw prefixes.

References and links
- Confluence draft: https://redwood-confluence/internal/INF-PA-42
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1189 (warm-pools prototype)
- Simulation JIRA: JIRA-INF-7213

End of scratchpad (for now). Will iterate after running offline replays and talking to Marco about warm pool sizing.
